brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.requirement: A planter for a kitchen windowsill
requirements.evidence: Three hex base pieces in a straight row (piece at cells -1,0 / 0,0 / 1,0), each holding a drained full-depth bin (hex-bin-full-drain), joined by two joint bolts. check_build: meshClash clear, LOOSE_BODY cleared, no errors.
Each bin is filled with soil and planted: basil-young at -1,0; chives-young at 0,0; thyme-young at 1,0. No PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL warnings.

The footprint is a 3-cell row about 190 mm wide that fits a sill, and the drain bins allow water to leave. The configurator does not model sunlight, heat or UV, so suitability for a sunny sill and the durability of the printed material outdoors are not verified; the user must choose a suitable material.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three hex bases in a row, each with a drained bin filled with soil, carrying basil, chives and thyme (young stage). Joint bolts lock the row and check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Sun exposure and material durability are not something the configurator can check.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
